utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Welcome back. If there are no procedural matters, the witness should be brought in. No, there are procedure matters. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to Defence. Good afternoon, everyone. This should not interfere with the witness being brought in. It's very brief. I just wanted to announce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, the witness should be brought. Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just wanted to announce formally, I'd notified the parties and the Registry, I think, by e-mail last week that we will move to withdraw -- or we are moving to withdraw, orally, Witness 52. He was scheduled to testify via videolink next week. We've continued to review our witness list, pursuant to the Trial Chamber's instructions to do so, and the witness is somebody that we considered not essential. We thought we could save some time, and we have decided to withdraw that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Nikolic. Welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony last week still applies. Mr. Tolimir, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to greet everybody present in the courtroom. May this day and the whole trial end in accordance with God's will and not my will.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to greet Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We finished off last time with my promise to discuss the Green Order or, more precisely, the activities of UNPROFOR against the VRS in and around Srebrenica. My question is: Do you know that the UNPROFOR soldiers in Srebrenica received an order to engage in combat the units of the VRS on the 8th, 9th, and 10th of July? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such orders or, more precisely, any orders that the DutchBat would have received. And I also don't know this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At 3457 - that's the transcript page - of the 9th of July --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: -- Mr. Franken, the deputy commander of DutchBat in Srebrenica, said, quote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreter asked you to slow down, especially while reading. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I shall repeat the quote. Well, I've already said it: "Yes, we are at war with the VRS, and we opened fire together with the Muslim army." That's when I asked him: Was it your mandate to destroy the weapons that belonged to the VRS, and was it your mandate to go to war against the VRS after you received your so-called Green Order? And at page 3484, line 1 to 3, he answered: "No, it wasn't part of the mandate. However, my mandate was significantly changed at the moment when the UN ordered me to defend Srebrenica. That was one of the reasons why I issued the Green Order, and in that sense, he did." My question: Bearing in mind what the deputy commander said, and that was the deputy commander of Mr. Karremans, the person who commanded the units who were in combat against the VRS on the 8th, 9th, and 10th, could that be the reason why the UN soldiers, on the 8th, 9th, and 10th, were fleeing, trying to reach the VRS territory, what you then recorded in those two official notes that we've seen earlier? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, the 9th of July, 2010, is the wrong date. Mr. Franken testified on the 30th of June and the 1st and 6th of July, not on the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise if I misspoke. So he said that he issued the Green Order on the 9th of July, and I probably misread it and thinking that that was the day of his testimony. So he issued the order on the 9th of July. I'm going to repeat the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not necessary. The witness understood your question. Sir, do you recall the question of Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. General, sir, I can only assume -- I can only assume all those various reasons, including the reason that you just mentioned. I think that the first day of my testimony, when I was answering your question -- your questions, I also answered these questions: What were the reasons because of which a part of the members of the DutchBat crossed over to the Serbian side. I agree that the situation in Srebrenica, in those days when the combat was going on, was very difficult. I also agree that the DutchBat was in a very difficult situation. There was no way out for them, militarily speaking. Now I'm telling you my own opinion. I also agree that, militarily speaking, they had to opt for one of the sides. They were in Srebrenica. They were under pressure from the Muslims. And I'm convinced that they simply had to choose one of the sides and then act probably also against their own will because of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Did you maybe notice that Mr. Franken, at transcript 3484, also said that it wasn't part of their mandate, to open fire on the VRS and act together with the Muslim army? Will you consider that this is justified; that UNPROFOR, as a peacekeeping force, should act against one of the warring sides? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a rough idea about what was the mandate of the DutchBat in Srebrenica; not only the DutchBat, also all the previous peacekeeping forces that were there. I do not consider that their task that we are talking about now was something that was defined within their regular mandate. However, you have to agree with me that that situation was an extraordinary situation. And now I can only assume again -- I do not have facts, I cannot prove anything, but I assume that the DutchBat simply acted in accordance with the new situation. That is my opinion, the opinion of a person who took part in all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand you, but I want to ask you something else. Did you think all this then, while you were at the position, when your soldiers were under the fire of UNPROFOR and the Muslims, or is it something that you only think now? And, generally speaking, can it be said that the situation which arises is something that can give the right to change the mandate of the United Nations forces? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm absolutely against anybody taking the right to fight the forces that I belong to. That's quite obvious. But at the same time, I worked with them, I spoke to them, and up until that moment, up until that extraordinary situation, as far as I know, the UNPROFOR forces did not take one or the other side. They had problems with both sides. They had problems with the Muslims and the Serbs. And they did not take sides. So it was only this time. I emphasise that this was an exception; this was an extraordinary situation. They found themselves in that situation, and that's when they took sides. I do not justify that, I don't think it was good of them to do that, and I don't think that they should have done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, did those 30 soldiers who fled to the territory of Republika Srpska, did they see for themselves that their command wanted to send them to fight one side against the other? Did they say to both us and Muslims, Please do not force us to go and fight for one side and against the other? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time, I partially answered that question. I spoke to those people who fled and crossed over to the Serbian side. They told me why they did it, why they crossed over, and it is obvious that the main reason for them crossing to the Serbian side was the fact that they were threatened. They found themselves between the two warring sides. And another important aspect is the fact that the Muslim forces prevented them to withdraw from their observation posts, regardless of the combat situation. So they simply used this new situation, the fact that the Serbian forces advanced towards some of the observation posts, and most of them then fled over to the territory controlled by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you to answer my questions in a brief and succinct way. We are not defending UNPROFOR here. Whatever happened, whoever is competent to do that is going to decide what actually happened. My following question is: Do you know that not only UNPROFOR, but NATO as well, engaged the VRS in combat in Srebrenica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you and your brigade and the units around Srebrenica know that NATO was preparing a wider attack against the VRS and that in Srebrenica they were about to openly side with the Muslim side? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information that reached my brigade, and me personally, was that NATO was about to engage the forces of Republika Srpska which were in and around the enclave, although mostly at that moment they were already inside the enclave. I don't know and I did not have any information about how many air-strikes they were talking about. What we did know was that the NATO air forces were about to engage our positions, our materiel, our tanks, and everything else that was within the enclave on the axis of the attack.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at D137 in e-court. That's a document that speaks about the intention of NATO to act against the positions of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for that: Did you know that the Muslims were doing whatever they could to provoke NATO into action, but at the same time that they were trying to blame the Serb side for that? Did you have any information on that, any indicia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer in affirmative. I really don't know what the Muslims were doing in order to provoke those air-strikes. If you really want me to answer, I have to say I don't know, or, rather, what I did know, if that is sufficient --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It's all right. It's sufficient for me that you told me that you didn't know. Now, let us take a look at this document. "Srebrenica's Death Fields," documentary film of the radio/television of Serbia, broadcast on the 9th of July, 2010. And this is the transcript of a part of the conversation broadcast on the Serbian television on the 9th of July. Narrator: "On the evening of the 10th of July, a meeting between the Dutch Battalion commander and representatives of the 28th Division was held in the post office building in Srebrenica?" Hakija Meholjic, member of the Srebrenica War Presidency, 1993 to 1995, said: "In the meantime, Karremans arrived, requesting a meeting. I told him, Five more minutes so we can first agree on everything ourselves, because we have no reason to trust you anymore. We arranged everything. Then we received him for a talk. And he said that NATO informed him that a death zone has been set around Srebrenica for tomorrow at half past 5.00. Everything that moves on two, four, or a hundred feet, or on a hundred wheels, or on one wheel, or on two wheels, that it will be destroyed, that it will be destroyed." So that's what Hakija Meholjic said. Did you know Hakija Meholjic, the member of the Srebrenica War Presidency during the war in Srebrenica? He was a member of the War Presidency. Did you know him and did you know this? Did you have any information on this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Hakija Meholjic in person, but I knew him by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you can see here that he tells about what he had been told by Mr. Karremans; that he had been informed that everything will be destroyed around Srebrenica. Did you receive similar information or information to that effect from your own intelligence sources? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way you read it from this article and in this context -- in relation to this context, I personally had no such information, no information that a NATO attack was imminent against the Serb side and the Serbian materiel and technical equipment. Now, that anything that was moving was to be destroyed, I really had no such information. And this is the first time ever that I actually see that there was an interview of this type and that this information was provided. That there was a death zone to be in place around Srebrenica, I had no such information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the second paragraph to see what the other person who participated in this programme has to say, Hasan Nuhanovic, the UN interpreter in Srebrenica. He says the following: "The Serbian side was issued an ultimatum to withdraw by 0600 hours to their starting positions, in other words, to Zeleni Jadar, to go back six kilometres or they would be bombarded at 0600 hours. They said that the number of aircraft that will come for the air-strike, they told me, would be between 40 and 70. That is what they said." And then the narrator or the journalist says: "Well, the air-strikes did not start at 0600 hours, but rather at 1400 hours. The number of aircraft attacking the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska was not 40, but two." My question is this: Did you know Mr. Hasan Nuhanovic, this person mentioned here, who had this to say about the air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew this person. He was an interpreter, and he attended the various meetings which I attended as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he issue this ultimatum through you, or was it done some other way, as he mentions in this interview with him?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that I had anything to do with the ultimatum that had to do with the withdrawal of forces to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Later on, did you find out, did you learn, whether NATO had actually launched air-strikes, as it says here, and that two aircraft were used for that, and that it started at 1400 hours? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NATO aircraft did engage; they did carry out air-strikes during the day. I know that the positions of the Serb forces were under attack, as well as the tank forces, which were within the enclave. They were targets of these air-strikes. What I did see was that there were two or three aircraft that were involved, not more. And I recall another thing. I recall that the forces in the Pribicevic Sector actually tried to down the aircraft. They opened fire on them. I think this was the 2-S system. That's what it was called, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Now, I asked you a little earlier whether you knew what the Muslims did in order to instigate NATO to bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at D20, paragraph 3, page 58. So paragraph 3, 58, please. This is a debriefing. We don't have it before us yet. I won't start reading out until you actually have the text before you. We need paragraph 3.58, 3.58. Thank you. Could you please show paragraph 3.58 for the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now we have it before us, and let's see what it says: "On Monday, the 10th of July, the commander of OP-M received orders from the C-Company commander to co-ordinate with the BiH. That evening, fighting broke out among the BiH soldiers, resulting in dead and wounded. At around noon on Tuesday, 11th of July, a number of shells struck the area near the armoured vehicles. The abandoned OP was also shelled. Chaos prevailed among the BiH. Internal fighting broke out once again. That evening, the OP crew were permitted to leave because they were willing to take the wife and children of a local BiH leader with them. When the two BiH soldiers with the anti-tank weapons attempted to prevent their departure, they were shot in the head by the BiH leader. This led, once again, to fighting between the BiH soldiers. En route to Potocari, they picked up many refugees. They came under fire on two more occasions. At 0130 hours on Wednesday, 12th of July, they arrived in Potocari, where they joined the B-Company positions to the south of the compound." Now, I read this out because I'd like to put a question to you. Did you know that there was fighting amongst the Muslims themselves, that there were incidents, and that some soldiers were even killed on such occasions? Did you know of that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it would be fair to the witness to tell him what you did read from. You just said, "This is a debriefing," but it's a lengthy document and you should tell the witness who is the author of it and what kind of debriefing this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we show the first page of this document for the witness. And in the meantime, I will tell him as you instructed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As you can see, it says here that this is a report based on the debriefing on Srebrenica, and it was done in Assen on the 4th of October, 1995. This is a report by the soldiers in Srebrenica, members of UNPROFOR who were deployed in Srebrenica during the events. And in this debriefing they provided their own statements and recounted the developments there. Now, I just read out a portion of this report that related to the 10th, 11th, and 12th. Thank you. And my question was -- and I believe that the witness was aware of this because he had heard of this, because he was in contact with some of these people. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be as precise as I can be. At the time of the events, I did not know what was going on, nor could I have. I didn't know what was happening between the UNPROFOR members and the Muslim soldiers. Later on, I did hear of the in-fighting in the BiH ranks and the fighting between -- the clashes between the BiH soldiers and the UNPROFOR members. Later on, I also heard that there had been a person killed and that a transport across the Yellow Bridge was organised to take out the body of this soldier who had been killed. Of course, I learnt of all of this later on. But what I clearly recall is that at the time when the operation began, up until the fall of the enclave, I was prohibited -- and I don't know about others, but I was prohibited from getting in touch with the DutchBat forces, and that they never requested a meeting with the Serb side. That's what I clearly recall. As for the other matters that you mentioned, the clashes, the wounding, the killing of this soldier, I learnt of that later on. But at the time of the events themselves, I had no idea of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. Now I would like to read to you D20. That's on page 46, the same document, the debriefing, paragraph 4.13. That deals with activities of the BiH Army during the attack on the enclave, and this, too, is based on the debriefing on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see paragraph 4.13.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, General, sir, but I did not have the B/C/S, the translation of this document, before me, so I could not read it out for myself. I couldn't follow what was being said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, no, there is no translation, but that's why I will read this out to you. That will be the translation. So I'll read this paragraph: "BiH soldiers, complete with blue caps or blue hats, came within a distance of 15 metres from one of the observation posts. They opened fire from this position in the direction of the BSA front-line, resembling UN personnel so that it seemed as if the UN had opened fire. In this way, they attempted to draw fire from the BSA on the OP and thus involve DutchBat in combat actions." End of quote of paragraph 4.13. I've read it out because we don't have a translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just ask if we could see the page in its entirety. I don't know if there's a particular date or time-period that's attached to this paragraph. I just wanted to see, because we got the list too late to be able to grab the documents before court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you able to figure out the time-frame? The heading -- headline of this part is: "Misuse of Uniforms," and I think it seems to be a kind of summary of different events at different dates, so that we can't figure out that at the moment. That may be checked at a later time. Sir, Mr. Tolimir, now put your question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is Exhibit D20. It had already been disclosed to the Prosecution earlier, and it has already been admitted into evidence. This relates to Srebrenica, and paragraph 4.13 relates to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have heard all this. Please continue and put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps I should tell this for the witness's benefit. What was voiced here by the Prosecutor was doubts about whether this related to the events in Srebrenica, so let me put this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did you ever hear that Muslim soldiers would put on UNPROFOR uniforms and pretending or resembling UNPROFOR members in order to actually draw fire and provoke UNPROFOR action against Serbs? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will try to describe exactly what this is a reference to, and I think that will make it clearer. It is true; namely, what Mr. Tolimir has mentioned is true to the extent that the Muslim forces -- but I have to say that this was actually the case throughout the time when UNPROFOR came to the protected zone or protected area of Srebrenica, so from the very start. So now let me talk about the beginning and the way things worked. The UNPROFOR forces organised, and they organised defences within the enclave. I don't have the map before me, but I did have the names earlier, I had seen them. There were 10 check-points that they kept under control. Most of them were on elevated -- elevations around Srebrenica, dominant positions around Srebrenica. Now, Muslims kept taking up position between these check-points, between two check-points, for instance, on the ground, and from those positions they provoked the Serbian side. They opened fire on them, in that way provoking the Serb sides to respond to their fire. This -- and when I say "fire," I mean mortar fire, infantry weapons fire. But I don't recall that before the conflict itself they had ever used the peacekeeping forces' uniforms. I don't recall there ever being any talk about that, this kind of abuse, the abuse of the uniform. But the abuse of the check-points, that was something that we discussed. So after the attack, on those critical days when the Serb forces entered the enclave, it is possible that in those days and in that situation they had also gotten hold of uniforms, because at that time some of those check-points had already been abandoned and the equipment of the DutchBat forces that had been kept there remained there. So it is possible, and I see that as the only possibility, that when the DutchBat soldiers withdrew from those check-points, that they actually seized those uniforms and then used them. So that's all I would know about this particular abuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic, for clarifying this. Now, can I refer you to paragraph 4.14, where it describes how Muslim soldiers would frequently wear civilian clothes and then they would put on uniforms and then they would go back to civilian clothes and so on. So we can see here that it says: "There were also instances that BiH Army soldiers could not be identified as personnel, military personnel, because DutchBat personnel had recognised some people who had mingled in civilian clothing among the refugees moving from Srebrenica to Potocari or when they were on the compound in Potocari. Local women known to be members of the BiH were also seen later in civilian clothing." Thank you. So my question is: Did you know -- did you have any information to the effect that Muslim forces, for the most part, moved in uniforms in order to show to the UNPROFOR forces that there were no -- that there was no military personnel in the enclaves?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is what we heard the accused say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that, by this question, you asked me if I had information that members of the 28th Division wore civilian clothing. The interpretation I had was "military clothing," but I think it has to do with them wearing civilian clothing. I had information, as well as the Dutch Battalion, not only in this phase during the phase of the attack on the enclave, but also in the prior phase when there was no indication of any attacks, when we still had the provocations that I spoke about in my answer to the previous question. What happened was that most often they appeared in civilian clothing. They would fire from those positions in the area between the two check-points, and then they would pull back. And then the Dutch, in their conversations with me, frequently complained about this occurrence, that they were unable to implement the control and that they couldn't differentiate between civilians and those who were actually military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. If you noticed, in the last sentence of paragraph 4.14, it states: "Local women known to be members of the BiH were also seen later in civilian clothing." My question is: Did you have information about there were members of the BiH women in the Srebrenica area who were members of the 28th Division of the B&H Army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can talk about what my assessments were. And they were -- actually, I felt that there were women in the armed forces, but I never expected them to be in the combat part. It was just like in my brigade; there were some women who were engaged on certain posts. But, believe me, other than one name that was mentioned, I don't believe that women in Srebrenica were engaged as fighters in the 28th Division. I didn't have information of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right, thank you. But can you tell us about that one instance that you know of, that you're familiar with the name? Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what you know about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That woman is called Esma Kiveric. I know that woman from before the war, personally. We were on good terms. She used to work with my wife, at the same school. And there was some stories going around, in any case, that she took part in these various attacks and massacres. In particular, there was an attack that was mentioned on the village of Bjelovac. I really never had any valid arguments or confirmation that she really was there. These were just stories that I heard. Later, nothing was confirmed in relation to this Esma Kiveric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Since you've just mentioned this place, Bjelovac, and you also referred to it in your statement on page 49. We can look at it. This is your statement 65 ter 724 -- 7274 provided to us by the Prosecution. This is the 65 ter number. It's page 49, line -- it's page 49, line 9. You mention Bjelovac and Kravica. Could you explain more broadly what you meant when you talk about Bjelovac and Kravica? Actually, it's page 53 in the English. "Persons were indicated who had attacked Bjelovac, where there were 106 dead civilians, and then there were some other Serb villages outside of the enclave. Now the indications need to be proved." And then later the investigator didn't ask you about that, so you didn't speak any more about that. So this is an opportunity for you to tell us what exactly happened in Bjelovac and Kravica and other Serb villages outside of the enclave. If you can explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain, briefly, events from each of the villages. When we're talking about Bjelovac, we're talking about an attack by the Muslim forces from the Srebrenica area, under the command of Naser Oric. This was an attack on a village that was in the Bratunac municipality territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, and the same thing for Kravica. This is an event involving an attack on the Serbian Orthodox Christmas, the 7th of January, 1993. It was an attack on the Serbian village of Kravica from the Srebrenica area by Muslim forces under the command of Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us how many victims there were in Bjelovac and how many in Kravica, and are both of those villages part of the Bratunac municipality, where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. The villages of Kravica and Bratunac [as interpreted] were villages in the Bratunac municipality. From what I can recall, there were some 46 or 48 victims in Kravica. I don't remember exactly, but I do have that information. And there were 106 dead in the village of Bjelovac, soldiers, civilians, women, others also.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please tell us whether this was one of the reasons why the population of Bratunac was uncomfortable in their feelings about Muslims and would not accept them to be in their area? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the sake of truth, I would like it to be known here that the Serbs were in Bratunac, the Muslims were in Srebrenica. In that wartime period, so many killings occurred and so much blood was shed that Muslims in that area and Serbs hated each other. I mean, I cannot put it in any nicer terms. There was so much hatred in that area between those two peoples that it was really incredible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber how many other villages were targets of attacks that were carried out on Fakovici, Rakovici, and other surrounding villages? I don't want to mention all of them. I'm not sure that I even have all the relevant concerning them.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you made a slip of the tongue. Perhaps you didn't, but I think that you did. These villages were not attacked from within the enclave. Let's be completely clear. The village of Kravica was attacked before Srebrenica was declared an enclave. So the attack did not happen after it was proclaimed an enclave. The attack on Bjelovac also did not take place later when the international forces arrived and when Srebrenica was declared an enclave. These attacks that you mention, it's true that many villages were attacked. I can list each village and hamlet in my municipality that was attacked. However, the bulk of the attacks were carried out at the beginning of the war, in 1992, up until the international peacekeeping forces arrived at Srebrenica. If you're interested about that, I can talk about it. I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can tell us, I would ask you to tell us, briefly, in a few sentences, something about that, because it's important for that area and for the whole situation that your unit and the place where you were happened to be in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of my municipality, the municipality of Bratunac, other than the urban part, I can state that the urban area encompassed some four kilometres from the centre of town, it was that area, and then this was encircled by an area that was not destroyed, not captured, not attacked. Then in my territory, there's another area which is a part along the Drina River towards Zvornik, and that's where there are villages that were not attacked. Everything else in my territory, if we start in order from Skelani, they were attacked, destroyed, torched. There were casualties. Then Rakovici, Fakovici, Stamatovici [phoen], Ducici; I don't need to list all of them. All the villages that are in the area of Srebrenica were attacked, other than these two villages that I spoke about in the area some four kilometres away from the centre of town and along the River Drina. All the other villages were attacked, torched. And in each of these villages there were military and civilian casualties, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did this later have the result that this agreement was subsequently signed, because when the army from Republika Srpska began defending those villages, an agreement was later signed in May -- we can look at D21 now so you can find it easier to answer. This is an agreement on the demilitarisation or cease-fire in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, signed between Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic and General Sefer Halilovic on the 8th of May, 1993. Now you can see the document. It's signed by UNPROFOR Commander Philippe Morillon as well, General Halilovic, and General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can look at page 2 in the Serbian now, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, you and I know what happened in 1993 in this period. But for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I would just like to say something to make the situation clear. Previously, we talked about the situation in that period. With the signing of the agreement proclaiming Srebrenica a safe zone -- actually, this was preceded by an offensive by our forces in the spring of 1993. In my units, my brigade's AOR, the Serbian forces reached Srebrenica, itself. They reached a position called Crni Guber. And we needed just one more day to enter Srebrenica. And that is when -- I don't know who made the decision. I was in the field then, in the Pribicevac area. Then when in the evening sometime an order came to cease all further action and any further engagement in relation to Srebrenica and that Serbian forces should entrench at positions they had reached so far, all I knew at the time is that this order came from the Main Staff Command and from the president of the republic, even. I didn't see the order, myself, but it reached me at my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether the area where the Muslims were was reduced only to the urban area, because you only needed some two or three kilometres more in order to enter the town? Was the area occupied by the Muslim forces reduced to the city or the town area only? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree with what you assert but only in that area where the main thrust of the attack was, that area of Crni Guber on that southern side. Actually, no, it's not the southern side. Actually, it's just from that entrance or approach to Srebrenica. That is -- for that part, I can give you an affirmative answer. However, Serbian forces were not advancing in a circle uniformly towards town from all sides, so we cannot say that it was reduced to an urban area some four kilometres away from the city centre. I am talking about that part, and I am stating affirmatively that that applied to the Crni Guber area. But if we're talking about Crni Buljin and other areas, I would like to note that we did not come that close to the enclave. We had stopped at the lines we had reached at that point. And after Srebrenica was proclaimed a safe zone, we stayed at those lines that we had attained.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As the forces that had almost entered Srebrenica, were you told that the Muslims accepted the cease-fire and the demilitarisation of the zone and that they would stop further action and that they were asking for a cease-fire? Were you informed about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was clear at the time, at least from what we were told at our positions at the time, that any advance was being halted, all attacks on Srebrenica were being halted, and that the Muslims had accepted a truce and a cease-fire. And just for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I would like to say that in that period when a cease-fire was requested and when it really did take hold and from what I could see in that period during those days when I was at Pribicevac, that's in that area, you could see vast movements of civilians between Srebrenica going in the direction of Zepa, and so on and so forth, so that the cease-fire was accepted by the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the proposal by the Muslim side to accept the evacuation of the Muslim population who wanted to go to Tuzla, was it also accepted at the time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know for sure is that there was a possibility for all those who wanted to leave the enclave of Srebrenica, and I'm speaking here about civilians, had the opportunity to do so. Serbian side guaranteed that they would be able to cross through their territory, through Bratunac, and further on where they wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that a certain number of inhabitants did leave at the time and that there were convoys taking them over to the territory controlled by the BiH Army? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I think it was sometime by the end of 1993 or the beginning of 1994. A large number of Muslim civilians from Srebrenica -- I used to have more precise data; I think there was about 3.000 to 4.000 of them. They left the Srebrenica enclave, escorted by the Serbian side, and they crossed over to the free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Muslims often want to go, legally or illegally, and leave Srebrenica to reach the territory controlled by the BiH Army or, more precisely, the Central Bosnia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember best is that there were many requests made through UNPROFOR, International Military Observers, ICRC, and similar organisations, so requests to the effect that certain families wanted to cross to the Muslim-controlled territory would come in all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember your reports in which you said that they also use numerous illegal channels to move through Zepa or through other corridors that they carved out themselves and that they were leaving Srebrenica, going towards Kladanj, Tuzla, and other parts of Bosnia controlled by the Muslim side? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I used to send reports to my superior command, the Drina Corps Command. I knew that civilians from Srebrenica were using also those channels that you call illegal channels. It's basically a route going across Ravni Buljin, Bokcin Potok, Nova Kasaba, and further on across Cerska. Or they would also go towards Udrc and in the direction of Tuzla. They were using all sorts of various ways. But, generally speaking, I always reported that we had such information and that from the positions of the Bratunac Brigade in the area of Ravni Buljin it was possible to see that movement directly and the movements towards Zepa, towards Kladanj, and towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic, did you have any information that the Muslims from Srebrenica used the corridor Buljin-Cerska-Baljkovica, the same corridor used later on when they attempted a breakthrough from Srebrenica? Did you have any intelligence information on that particular corridor? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I mentioned those corridors in all my reports, but I do know that they did use those corridors. When I wrote my memos, I would probably mention one of the corridors, depending on the information I had at my disposal at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to waste time by showing you all those documents, but I would like to ask you to take a look at the document that is currently on the screen. It's D21. I would like to take a look at page 3, Article 3, which is entitled "Demilitarisation." It speaks about the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa. And in Article 3, we find, I quote: "Every military or paramilitary unit will have either to withdraw from the demilitarised zone or to submit/hand over their weapons. Ammunition, mines, explosives, and combat supplies in the demilitarised zones will be handed over/submitted to UNPROFOR. "After submission/hand over of all weapons, ammunition, mines, and combat supplies in the DMZ, the contracting parties will declare that the demilitarisation is complete." And then it says that in Srebrenica it has to be done by Monday, the 10th of May, 1993, by 1700 hours; and in Zepa, by the 12th of May, by 1700 hours. End quote. My question is: Bearing in mind this agreement, did the Muslims have the duty to hand over all the weapons and leave the demilitarised zone, if we are talking about armed forces, paramilitary groups, or military groups? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, I wouldn't like to ascribe to myself the importance that I do not have. I'm reluctant to comment on this agreement. It speaks for itself. I think that any comment coming from me would be moot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. You can tell us what you know. Did you report that the Muslims did not demilitarise that zone at all, that they were still moving within the zone and attacking the territory, the civilians, and the units within the zone? Do you remember that you used to send reports about that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that I used to send reports all the time, reports on this topic. I remember that Srebrenica was not a demilitarised zone, that the Muslims within Srebrenica were not disarmed, and that from that enclave they carried out incursions, sabotage excursions, attacks, ambushes, and other things. And it is also important to say that I also spoke about those matters with the DutchBat members, and it was their duty to prevent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did General Zivanovic at any point request you to protest with the UNPROFOR forces and to contact them about the activities that were going on within the demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there were such protests that I made based on the request of General Zivanovic or maybe even request from the Main Staff. I remember that I used to protest in the written form and also verbally. I think that that was even a more frequent occurrence. Whenever I would meet up with the members of the DutchBat, I would always convey our concern to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us: Do you remember that from the beginning of 1995 the Main Staff and General Zivanovic were telling both to UNPROFOR and the Muslims to stop the activities that were carried out from within the demilitarised zone and that we would, on the contrary, that we would be forced to prevent such activities? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that I was present every time when General Zivanovic was in the zone of responsibility of my brigade, but I was certainly present in 95 per cent of the cases, which means that I was present at the meetings between General Zivanovic and the representatives of DutchBat. They spoke about exactly those issues. And he would then request the DutchBat to prevent the incidents and the incursions that were caused by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look at 1D655. That's a statement made by General Smith. He says that General Mladic mentioned on a number of occasions incidents caused by Muslims in Srebrenica, and he describes the situation. Can we have 1D655, paragraph 17. It's D192. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do we have D192 on the screen now? Thank you. And can you help me, Mr. Tolimir. Is that an OTP statement, or what is it about?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is a statement by General Smith, and it was given to the Dutch Investigation Centre, NIOD. He described our subject matter in paragraph 17. This witness is aware of the NIOD because he was in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Tolimir, you will recall that the witness said this is a summary of what he has told NIOD, and he didn't sign anything. Just to have it clear on the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is what General Smith said. I quote from paragraph 17. This is what he said to the NIOD but then he denied it at the trial: "The first meeting with Mladic after the fall of Srebrenica on Sunday, the 16th of July, was also attended by Milosevic, Bildt, Akashi, and Janvier. Smith had a big quarrel with Mladic." And so on and so forth. I quoted this so that you could see when it took place. And now let us take a look at what General Smith says in a statement of his that he did not deny. Can we have 65 ter 7247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And this is now D193.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now let us take a look at what he says in a statement that he did not repudiate. It is 65 ter 7247. Thank you. Can we have page 9, paragraph 4 on page 9. Can we zoom in so that the witness can see. This is where the statement goes. It's page 9, paragraph 4: "Mladic said that his concern about Bosnian army's intentions had led him to restrict the amount of food, medicine, and fuel for the enclaves, and claimed that the United Nations was supplying the Bosnian army. I replied that any attack on the UN safe areas would be condemned by the international community and would risk a response by NATO air power against the Bosnian Serbs. This brought forward a tirade of threats of counter-action from Mladic."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: Did you know that General Mladic told UNPROFOR on a number of occasions that there were attacks going on from within the enclave against his forces and that he claimed that UNPROFOR was protecting the Muslim attackers within the enclave? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me whether I knew that General Mladic was doing that, then my answer is no. I wasn't close to General Mladic. I didn't know what he was doing. I can answer about our common position. I can tell you about my reports to my corps command and to the Main Staff. We were dissatisfied by the fact that the enclave had not been disarmed and by the fact that there were attacks and provocations from the enclave. That's what I know. That's what I did at my level. Now, whether I was aware of the general position of the VRS, represented by General Mladic, I can say, yes, I was aware of this general discontent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Then let's take a look at the second paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] can we move page 9 a little bit so that we can see the second paragraph on this page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see it now, where it says, I quote: "During the returning from Srebrenica to Sarajevo on the 7th of March, I met with Mladic, at his request, at the hotel in Vlasenica. Mladic was accompanied by Major General Zivanovic, commander of the Drina Corps, and Lieutenant-Colonel Kralj, an intelligence officer." That's what he says. Kralj was actually the liaison officer for UNPROFOR. "At the meeting, Mladic again stated that he would continue to delay convoy access -- to deny convoy access to the enclaves as long as the Bosnian Serbs remained under sections. The second issue Mladic discussed was to link an UNPROFOR withdrawal from the UNPAs in Croatia with a demand for a UN withdrawal from all enclaves in Bosnia. The third and most important issue discussed was the demilitarisation of the safe areas of Gorazde, Srebrenica, and Zepa." So bearing all this in mind, my question is: Your corps commander, Zivanovic, and General Mladic, the commander of the Main Staff, did they draw the attention of General Smith, way back on the 7th of March, to the fact that it was necessary to do something about the activities from the enclaves and to link it up with the withdrawal of the UN forces from the UN protected areas in Croatia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that this issue was on the table all the time. I cannot speak about specific meetings and this specific detail that you just read out, but, generally speaking, there was a constant dissatisfaction related to the status of Srebrenica as a protected area and everything that was going on around it, including the convoys, the restrictions, and everything else that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us, do you know that at that time there was an announcement that UNPROFOR would be withdrawn from the protected areas in Croatia, the areas where Serbs lived, and that that was the reason for the request for them to withdraw from similar areas in Bosnia, that was the reason why you were asked about it, and also a part of an item was read out to you which ended with: "... in case of UNPROFOR withdrawal"? Do you remember that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this was quite a complicated and compound question. Could you please simplify this question for a better understanding for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you know that the VRS demanded the withdrawal of UNPROFOR from Srebrenica and Zepa in case of the withdrawal of UNPROFOR from the protected areas in Croatia? They wanted that the zones belonging to the Serbs and to the Muslims enjoy the same kind of protection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Related to this issue, I can only speak as an ordinary citizen. I had no information about what was going on and what was being demanded at the level of the Main Staff and General Mladic. However, as a person who was well informed, I can tell you that I did know about these activities and about Croatia. Of course, I didn't know details, and I did not know that the VRS related the two issues and also expanded it to the context of the enclaves in Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde. That, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us take a look at paragraph 3 to see what Mr. Smith had to say about it. It's the eighth line from the bottom, where it says: "During this explanation, he drew up a diagram about what he was prepared to accept as the borders of the protected areas. He drew up the document that is kept in the UN archives. His view was that the safe areas were strictly limited in Srebrenica to an area of 4.5 kilometres by 1 kilometre; at Gorazde, a radius of 1.5 kilometres from the centre of the built-up area; and at Zepa, an area 2.5 by 0.8 kilometre. Mladic then explained that he expected a Bosnian attack from the eastern enclaves and in this event he would attack into the enclaves to destroy the Bosnian army but would respect his (Mladic's) interpretation of the boundaries of the safe areas and not the UN's." Thank you. A moment ago, we saw that all armed formations, paramilitary and others, were supposed to leave the zone and that no weapons were supposed to remain within the zone, except with UNPROFOR. And now when General Mladic requests to reduce this area to four and a half kilometres, you were asked during your examination-in-chief why that happened. Well, do you see here that General Mladic officially submitted this proposal to UNPROFOR and that this could not be the subject of your criminal responsibility? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see what you just read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it unusual that there were attacks coming out from the zones that were supposed to be demilitarised? Was it unusual that the Muslims carried out attacks from those so-called demilitarised zones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question. Did you ask whether it was permitted or -- well, of course. No attacks were supposed to come out of the demilitarised zones, or anything like what was actually happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at the last paragraph that is visible on the screen, that's the fifth paragraph, where it says: "At the end of this series of meetings, I had come to the conclusion that the Bosnian Serbs had concluded that further fighting was inevitable and that they had to reach some form of conclusion within the year. The eastern enclaves were too strong and the Bosnian army within them constituted a clear threat, particularly as the BSA felt that they were likely to face attacks on multiple fronts: In the enclaves, the UN were being used as a shield by the Bosnians and a hostage by the Serbs." This was a quote from a statement given by the UNPROFOR commander for Bosnia and Herzegovina, General Smith. My question is: Were his estimates about the strength of the BiH Army forces within the so-called demilitarised zone of Srebrenica realistic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one thing that I didn't see. Here we see a specific estimate by General Smith, and it seems to me that I did not understand from this document what this estimate relates to and what forces he's describing. But I can tell you what I know. I can tell you what I did at my level. If Mr. Smith mentions strong forces, he is perfectly right. There were very strong forces within the Srebrenica enclave. At the time that the enclave was proclaimed, it was an operative group, and later on it was the 28th Division, which was still being formed. And they were, without a doubt, very strong and very dangerous forces in the territory where my unit was engaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you will have realised that we are over time now, five minutes too late already. We must have our first break now, and we will resume 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, I'd like to show you D16 now. Can we have D16, please. That is a document from the BH Army, dated the 17th of February, where even they report on their activities which were the subject of requests for demilitarisation. Now we have it before us. Take a look at the second paragraph, the fourth line, where it begins with the word: "The aggressor" on the 16th of February: "The aggressor, on the 16th of February, 1995, filed a request with UNPROFOR to declare Zepa a non-demilitarised zone, with the following rationale: "Because BH Army helicopter flights supplying weapons and ammunition have been registered; "Movements of the BH Army have been registered in the Zepa Sector; "Accusing members of the Ukrainian Battalion that they are covering up for the activities and intentions of the BH Army ... "On the night between the 15th and 16th February 1995, our helicopters were seen flying over and that infantry fire was opened on them ..." And so on and so forth. And here in this document, the third paragraph below, it says: "On the 17th of February, 1992, a helicopter reconnaissance of the Zepa zone was scheduled, but the aggressor did not allow it." And then it says -- and so on and so forth. Now --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, but, General, sir, could you please just point out the paragraph that you're referring to, because what you've just asked me about, I couldn't find any of that in there. So could you please show it to me, exactly where it is, so that I can read it for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Take a look at the second paragraph from the top, the paragraph beginning with the words: "The aggressor," and then answer my question. I will put a question to you so that you can answer it. Did the Serb side, through you or via the Main Staff, submit requests to the BH Army, requesting that they demilitarise the zones in keeping with the Agreement on the Demilitarisation Zones of 1993 that was signed by General Morillon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, did you find the relevant part now? You see the cursor there on the screen. Perhaps that indicates where Mr. Tolimir is reading from and to which part he is referring to. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I've just seen it. "On the 16th of February," and then "the aggressor," and so on. If that's the relevant part, yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now please look at the paragraph below: "On the basis of the aforementioned, the aggressor informed the Sarajevo Sector UNPROFOR Command that unless Zepa was declared a demilitarised zone, they would start offensive combat operations within seven days. "The ultimatum expires on the 23rd February 1995." Thank you. Can you see these two paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As the liaison officer for UNPROFOR, did you inform the UNPROFOR of all of this, in view of the fact that it was under the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to clarify something. I was not a liaison officer for my corps, but, rather, just for the Bratunac Brigade. There was another liaison officer who was responsible and appointed as the liaison officer by the Drina Corps. And to answer your question, every time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you answer this question, we didn't receive the interpretation of this question. And, therefore, it would be, for a better understanding of the transcript, better if you could please repeat your question, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My apologies, Mr. Nikolic. I misspoke when I said that he was a liaison officer of the corps. It's correct that -- what he said here, that it was in fact the Bratunac Brigade that he was the liaison officer of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So is it true that as the liaison officer of the Bratunac Brigade you launched protests on several occasions to the UNPROFOR, requesting that those zones be demilitarised and that soldiers be removed from them so that no incursions or raids could be conducted from within the zones?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that I sent, on countless occasions, protests, both on behalf of my brigade and of the superior command that actually charged me with that task and insisted on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see 1D658. 1D658, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That is a document from the Drina Corps Command, sent on the 23rd of March, 1995, to the UNPROFOR Command, Srebrenica Enclave. And this was to be handed in via the Bratunac Brigade and Captain Nikolic. And it says there: "The withdrawal" -- The title, it says, "The Withdrawal of Muslim Formations Within the Srebrenica Enclave: Warning." And then it says within the document, itself, and I quote: "We are all convinced that you are here to keep peace in this area, and we truly appreciate this. However, we cannot tolerate the Muslim formations to willfully leave the enclave and engage in combat in areas outside of the enclave. In the interests of peace in this area, make sure (and you can do that) that the Muslims remain within the enclave protected by your forces. Otherwise, I will issue an order for the Muslim formation that are outside of the enclave be removed by force from our area." And then it goes on to say: "Via Colonel Vukota, inform me of the time-period within which you will accomplish this, and return the Muslims to Srebrenica enclave." We see that this was signed by Major General Milenko Zivanovic, and we can also see from this document that you were not responsible for this, you were not in charge of this, but, rather, this Colonel Vukota that is mentioned, Vukota Vukovic, who is mentioned in this document by General Zivanovic. Now, the question to you: Does this confirm what you've told us about this and also what General Smith testified about when he met on the 7th of April with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is obvious, from the content of this document, what this relates to. I can just confirm that, indeed, on countless occasions, it was insisted that these matters contained in the document be resolved. So there is nothing else I should add here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, let's take a look at D53. And I would actually like to tender the document we have on the screens into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I don't find it on your fourth version of your list of documents to be used with this witness. We received it during the first session. This is not on the list. Again, I would like to invite you to provide the other party and the Chamber with a complete list. That would be helpful. This document will be received. No, I think there is no translation. It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D658 shall be assigned Exhibit D205, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies, once again, for our omission, and I will look into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, we have before us D53. This is a document that was compiled on the 17th of June, 1995; in other words, a month before the Srebrenica events. This is a document from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Army, General Staff, and it was sent under the title "Preparations for Offensive Combat Operations: Order." And then in the first paragraph, it reads: "Pursuant to a verbal order issued by the commander of the General Staff of the BH Army and Army General Rasim Delic, and on the occasion of the great success achieved by units of the BH Army in the wide area around Sarajevo and Gorazde, as well as on the basis of intelligence that the aggressor forces command of the Protection Regiment in Han Pijesak is holding parts of its unit in reserve to intervene in the event of an attack by our forces from Zepa, I hereby issue the following order: "1. Execute all preparations in the Command of the 28th Land/Army Division to execute offensive combat operations with a view to liberating the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, over-extending the A/S and inflicting losses on them, co-ordinating action within the BH Army forces, carrying out operations in the broader Sarajevo area." And so on and so forth. My question: Did you have information about the Muslim forces being issued assignments to continue their active operations from within the so-called Srebrenica demilitarised enclave against Republika Srpska army units and on the territory under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska without or outside of the enclave? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have information about the intentions of the units that were within the Srebrenica enclave, and I think there is a document to that effect that I sent to the Drina Corps Command. It's a document called "Intelligence Assessment," where I describe and explain in detail all the information that I had collected about the operations and intentions of the BH army from inside the protected enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa. In addition, I also stress in that communication -- I discuss the forces of the 2nd Corps, and the 28th Division that was part of the corps; I described their strengths and the manpower levels. So I did have these assessments, and I forwarded them to the Drina Corps Command, which is where my duty ends, as far as that is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell us, just briefly: Were there a number of orders on activities from within the demilitarised zones against units of your brigade and the VRS? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, I cannot talk about that, whether there were any orders sent to the Muslim forces, because I don't know anything about that. I don't know what orders they issued to their units. What I can tell you about is what I did. And I, at the brigade level, did have information about their future intentions to be carried out from within the enclave, and that is something that I can confirm. As for their orders, I really don't know anything about that because I did not have occasion to either hear about it or to see their orders, or nor did I ever have a source that could confirm anything to that effect. So I don't recall, at this point in time, that I ever encountered anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You answered me correctly. I had asked you if you knew that; you said you didn't. Now I would like to show you a document that was presented, and I even have its translation into English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D726 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It's a conversation that you had with an investigator from -- the NIOD investigator, which covers the knowledge and information you had about this particular event.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please indicate the paragraph numbers in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 7 in the Serbian, page 5 in the English. It's paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We don't need to show a number of documents that were arriving at the unit because there is a conclusion here from that overall estimate and the conclusion is in English. I quote that paragraph 41 on page 5 in the Serbian and page 7 in the English. It states: "The exodus from the enclave took the VRS by surprise. They believed that Oric had gone to Tuzla in order to establish a corridor with Srebrenica from there. In this way, they would have tried to break through from both areas. In such a scenario, the 2nd Corps would leave from Crni Vrh. From the corridor created in this way, the Muslims would then sweep clean the remaining territory in the direction of the Drina River and cleanse it of all Serbs. The information that the VRS had, that this plan would be implemented between the 20th and the 25th of July, 1995, this was the reason Oric and other officers had left the enclave. N. does not know whether it was this information that determined the time of the VRS attack." Does this correspond to the content of those numerous information reports and assessments that you received -- actually, that you were sending to the superior command in your regular combat reports and your own separate intelligence reports? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The essence of my estimates and reports to the superior command is exactly what you have read out just now. That means -- let me summarise that once again, and I think I can be more precise. So, my estimates at the time were that Naser Oric, together with a part of the forces, had left the Srebrenica enclave and that he had moved to Tuzla. And also what was constantly a feature of my report were assessments that at the same time, by being engaged from the Srebrenica area and from Tuzla, the Muslim forces, in co-ordinated action, would act and cleanse that part of Podrinje of the Serbs. That was my general assessment, and that was the danger that I saw at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you continue: "According to N., all Muslim decisions about Srebrenica came directly from Sarajevo. The 2nd Corps was only responsible for executing the military plans. According to N., there was a conflict between Oric and the 2nd Corps. Oric was supposed to organise special units from the ranks of the 2nd Corps for the breakthrough from Tuzla. The 2nd Corps was not particularly interested in the organisation of such a corridor." My question is: According to our information, ours and yours, because you were providing us with information, was the prevalent view in Srebrenica that the Srebrenica enclave would link up with Tuzla as a consequence of action going from the direction of Srebrenica and from the direction of Tuzla? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my assessments, I always, almost always, underscored that that was the point of what could happen, actually, that the objective was for the forces from Srebrenica to link up with the forces of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show P1217, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have used 1D726; are you going to tender it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, we would like to tender it. Since we don't have any more time, we're not going to be reading from it anymore. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D726 shall be assigned Exhibit D206. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at P1217. We can see it on our monitors now. The title of the document, and it's a document by the Drina Corps Command of the 15th of May, 1995, so the title of the document is "Order to Stabilise Defence around Zepa and Srebrenica Enclaves and Establish Conditions for the Liberation of the Enclaves." This order was delivered to all the units placed around Srebrenica. I am reading "Enemy information," and that is the first paragraph in that section. I apologise. "According to information gathered, the Muslims are carrying out intensive preparations for offense operations from the greater area of Tuzla, Kladanj, and Srebrenica, and Zepa enclaves, with the basic goal of cutting the RS/Republika Srpska territory, connecting the non-enclaves with the central part, the so-called BiH, and to access the Drina River. Simultaneous offensive activities are expected from the area of Kladanj and Kalesija. They will intensify infiltration of the reconnaissance and sabotage groups before the offensive operations on a larger scale, fully using the in-between areas and natural vegetation." My question is: Were you aware of this assessment, and did your command, as well, receive this order to stabilise the situation around the enclaves? Were you informed about this data, as an organ in your command? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see from the document that this was also delivered to my brigade. I assume, therefore, that I was familiar with it. I cannot really speak about this document specifically, but I definitely did see this type of document, and I would inform myself or acquaint myself with the contents once I received the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this is the corps commander's order being sent to all the brigade commanders, is there a chance that your brigade commander informed you about the intelligence data that he had received from the superior command in the form of the order to stabilise the front around the enclaves? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The practice in my command was that the brigade commander, upon receipt of a document, in particular if it was an order of this type or any other kind of type, would inform the inner command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at the second paragraph of this -- the third line of this second paragraph: "About 200 soldiers were sent from Srebrenica to the area of Radava. Some 150 soldiers in the greater area of Podravanje were deployed, and the reconnaissance patrols were spotted in the areas of Petrovacka, Greda, Kupusina, and a permanent check-point in the Kupusina area for the purpose of closing the enclave and stabilising the defence around them in order to liberate the enclave." Are these locations that are mentioned in this order were in the zone of responsibility of your corps and outside of the Srebrenica demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to speculate. If I were to have the map in front of me and if I could really look at where these places are, then I could, in general, say that a large number of these places, based on what I could quickly gather, are in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. But let me tell you, since really I don't want to quote and I don't want to speculate whether all of them are outside of the enclave, because that is something that I would need a map for, and then I could be quite sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether the broader area of Podravanje, where some 150 of their soldiers were deployed, was in the AOR of the Drina Corps and outside of the demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
